revealed digital clubbing and course crepitations in the right infra-clavicular area. Heart examination
is normal (see image and report).
Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 100 /min Respiratory rate 25 /min Temperature 39 °C
Sputum culture: Mixture of aerobic and anaerobic organisms. What is the most likely mechanism for
the underlying condition?
A. Aspiration
B. Vegetation embolism
C. Bronchogenic carcinoma
D. Direct extension from infected chest wall

A 30-year-old woman with bronchial asthma developed worsening dyspnea and cough following
paint inhalation from neighborhood apartment. On examination, she is in respiratory distress, cannot
complete a sentence and cyanosed. Chest auscultation revealed reduced breath sounds in both sides
with short inspiratory and exploratory rhonchi (see lab results).
Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg Heart rate 130 /min Respiratory rate 20 /min Oxygen saturation 85 %
Test Result Normal Values
ABG HCO3- 24 22-28 mmol/L
ABG PCO2 7.8 4.7-6.0 kPa
pH 7.3 7.36-7.45
ABG P02 7.5 10.6-14.2 kPa
Which of the following is the best immediate action in management?
A. Intravenous magnesium infusion
B. Intravenous aminophylline infusion
C. Intubation and mechanical ventilation
D. Nasal continuous positive airway pressure ventilation

A patient with poorly controlled bronchial asthma developed hypertension, which of the following
antihypertensive medications is contraindicated?
A. Beta blocker
B. Calcium channel blocker
C. Angiotensin II receptor blocker
D. Angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitor

A 60-year-old man with advanced squamous cell bronchogenic carcinoma presents with massive
malignant right pleural effusion. He has been admitted several times with similar findings for which
he undergoes several therapeutic pleural taps. Which of the following is the next best option in
management?
A. Diuretics
B. Ultrafiltration
C. Chemical pleurodesis
D. Low salt human albumin

A 40-year-old woman presents with progressive dyspnea, dry cough and reddish nodular skin lesion
over both shins. On examination, she has palpable cervical lymph nodes and bilateral diffuse fine
crepitations in both lungs (see reports).
Chest radiograph: Diffuse bilateral interstitial infiltrates with bilateral hilar lymph nodes enlargement.
Purified protein derivative (PPD): Negative.
Cervical lymph node biopsy: Non-caseating granuloma.
Which of the following is the next best option in management?
A. Montelukast
B. Glucocorticoids
C. Anti-tuberculosis
D. Salmeterol inhaler

A 60-year-old man with post pulmonary tuberculosis bronchiectasis presents with massive
hemoptysis. Physical examination shows course crepitations in the right scapular area (see image).
Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?
A. Sedation
B. Pneumonectomy
C. Chest physiotherapy
D. Positioning on right lateral decubitus

A 78-year-old woman is admitted with fever and confusion due to pneumonia. The doctors decided
to start her IV antibiotics. However, her son, who is the next of kin, disagreed and argued that
antibiotics will cause more harm. What is the best way to deal with this situation?
A. Ignore the opinion of the son and give the antibiotics to save the patient
B. Counsel the son in the presence of the consultants
C. Respect the opinion of the next of kin
D. Take the opinion of the patient

A young woman with long-standing rheumatoid arthritis is diagnosed to have non-specific interstitial
lung disease. The physician decided to start her on oral glucocorticoid. However, the patient is
concerned about the side effects related to this treatment. What is the best approach to deal with
this situation?
A. Stress the importance of the treatment and give the patient time to decide
B. Inform the patient that refusing this treatment might cause death
C. Inform the patient that there is no alternative treatment
D. Tell the patient that most of the side effects are not serious

An elderly patient is diagnosed with pulmonary tuberculosis and started on anti-TB treatment. He
developed jaundice, which progressed to liver failure for which he was admitted to the Critical Care
Unit. His son was very angry and decided to complain against the treating team. What is the
appropriate response to the son?
A. Tell him that this incident can happen to anyone
B. Inform him that the doctors offered the right management
C. Advise him against complaining as there is no medical error
D. Calm him down and inform him that this incident will be investigated

An elderly patient who has poorly controlled bronchial asthma with repeated admission to the
hospital is found to be non-compliant with his medications. Which of the following is the most
appropriate action?
A. Tell the patient that it is not acceptable to disrespect the advice of doctors
B. As the patient is noncompliant, just keep him in the hospital
C. Involve the next of kin to help to give his medications as prescribed
D. Tell the patient that he might die if he does not comply with the medications

A 69-year-old man with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease on oxygen therapy for the last 5
years. Which of the following markers is most useful for monitoring the progression of this patient?
A. Oxygen saturations
B. Number of exacerbations per year
C. FEV1/FVC ratio
D. FEV1

A 31-year-old man with asthma complaining of increasing wheeze in the past few hours. He rarely
attends asthma clinic and his previous best peak flow readings has been 400 L/min. Which of the
following would suggest acute severe asthma?
A. 02 saturation <95%
B. Respiratory rate >25
C. Carotid pulse > 100 bpm
D. Peak flow rate <300 L/min

A 38-year-old woman presents for annual asthma review. Her symptoms are very well controlled and
she has not had any attacks since her last review a year ago and has not used her salbutamol inhaler
once in that year. She is prescribed an inhaled beomethasone steroid twice daily in addition to her
salbutamol inhaler. What is the most appropriate next step in modifying her medication?
A. Add a leukotriene receptor antagonist
B. Double the dose of the inhaled corticosteroid
C. Stop both the salbutamol and becomethasone inhalers
D. Half the beclomethasone dose and review in 6 months

A 38-year-old man is admitted with a sudden onset dyspnoea and pleuritic chest pain. He is a smoker
but has no history of respiratory disease. He considers himself healthy and regularly plays football.
On admission, he has a chest x-ray that shows a pneumothorax with a 3cm rim of air. Aspiration is
successful and he is discharged. A follow-up chest x-ray 2 weeks later shows a complete resolution.
What is the single most important piece of advice to reduce his risk of further pneumothoraces?
A. Stop smoking
B. Avoid flying for 12 months
C. Avoid sports for 12 months
D. Arrange a course of respiratory physiotherapy pnemothorax

A 28-year-old wood worker presents to the clinic complaining of episodic shortness of breath. He
describes feeling wheezy and having a tendency to cough. A diagnosis of occupation asthma is
suspected. Which of the following is the most appropriate diagnostic investigation?
A. Serial peak flow measurements at work and at home
B. Specific IgE measurements
C. Skin prick test
D. Patch testing

A 66-year-old man presents with shortness of breath. He smokes 20 cigarettes/day but is otherwise
well. Spirometry shows a restrictive picture. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A. Pulmonary fibrosis
B. Bronchiectasis
C. Heart failure
D. Asthma

A 31-year-old man came for smoking cessation support as his father has recently been diagnosed
with lung cancer. He has a past medical history of epilepsy, which is well-controlled on
carbamazepine. Which smoking cessation medication would be contraindicated for this patient?
A. Nicotine replacement therapy
B. E-Cigarettes
C. Varenicline
D. Bupropion

A 51-year-old woman with asthma complaining of increasing shortness of breath and wheeze in the
past few hours. She has a long-standing diagnosis of asthma but her medication history suggests a
lack of compliance. Her best peak flow measurements in previous consultations have been 300 L/
min.
Which of the following features suggests acute severe asthma in this patient?
A. Heart rate 100/min
B. Respiratory rate >20/min
C. Peak flow rate 200 L/min
D. Inability to complete sentences in one breath

A 31-year-old man with asthma complaining of increasing wheeze in the past few hours. His
medication history suggests a lack of compliance. His best peak flow measurements in previous
consultations have been 600 L/min. Which of the following features suggests acute severe asthma in
this patient?
A. A peak flow rate of 250 L/min
B. Respiratory rate >20/min
C. Heart rate 100/min
D. SpO2 95%

A 22-year-old man, whose asthma is uncontrolled on beta agonist therapy, is commenced on a
steroid inhaler. Which of the following is the most likely adverse effect?
A. Dysphonia
B. Dental abscess
C. Peptic ulceration
D. Thrombocytopenia

A 58-year-old man presents with a 6-month history of breathlessness. He has been smoking all his
adult life, he smokes 10-15 cigarettes per day. On examination, he has lost the nail fold angle of his
fingers. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
B. Bronchial carcinoma
C. Aspergillosis
D. Asthma

A 36-year-old man with multiple health problems presents to the Emergency Department with an
episode of bronchospasm. He has a history of asthma and hypertension. He is undergoing a
medication review. Which of the following medications is most likely to be responsible?
A. Salmeterol
B. Atenolol
C. Ramipril
D. Aspirin

A 58-year-old man with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is ready to be discharged
home after acute exacerbation of the disease. Which of the following parameters indicate offering
long-term oxygen therapy?
A. 1 arterial blood gas measurement with p02 < 7,7 kPa
B. 2 arterial blood gases measurements with p02 < 7.3 kPa
C. 1 arterial blood gas measurement with p02 < 8.0 kPa
D. 2 arterial blood gases measurements with p02 < 6.3 kPa

A 22-year-old woman with cystic fibrosis presents with a 4-month history of weight loss, diarrhoea
and abdominal bloating. She has pale stools. There are no specific abnormalities on examination of
the abdomen other than she is clubbed with scattered chest crackles.
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A. Acute pancreatitis
B. Pancreatic carcinom
C. Pancreatic pseudocys
D. Chronic pancreatitis

A 59-year-old man comes to the clinic, with a 45 cigarette pack-year history, complaining of
breathlessness on exertion and a productive cough of white sputum over the last 6 months.
Cardiological investigations are normal (see report).
Spirometry: Shows an FEV1/FVC of 60% with minimal reversibility after a 2-week trial of oral steroids
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A. Asthma
B. Lung fibrosis
C. Left ventricular failure
D. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease

A 62-year-old woman is seen in the clinic with a history of weight loss, loss of appetite and shortness
of breath for the last 6 weeks. On examination, trachea is shifted to left side; there is reduced air
entry and duliness to percussion on the lower to midzones of the right lung.
Blood pressure 110/70 mmH
Heart rate 102 /min
Respiratory rate 22 /min
Temperature 37 °C
Oxygen saturation 91 %
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A. Right-sided pleural effusion
B. Right middle lobe pneumonia
C. Pulmonary embolism
D. Right pneumothorax

A 19-year-old man known to have asthma. He has never been admitted to hospital with an asthma
exacerbation and experiences symptoms once or twice a week but he is not on any medication.
Today he come to discuss the treatment options and he prefer to start medications only if needed
during the attacks. His peak expiratory flow reading is currently 85% of the normal predicted value
expected for his age and height.
Which of the following is the most appropriate first step in treatment?
A. Short-acting beta-2 agonist Inhaler
B. Long-acting beta-2 agonist inhaler
C. Leukotriene receptor antagonists
D. Low-dose steroid inhaler

A 40-year-old man diagnosed with pulmonary TB who started treatment 3 months ago, presents to
the clinic with a week's history of pins and needles in his hands and feet with associated numbness.
He tells that his symptoms started since he stopped taking the vitamins given to him
at the start of his TB treatment. Which of the following drugs is responsible for the symptoms
described by the patient?
A. Pyrazinamide
B. Ethambutol
C. Rifampicin
D. Isoniazid

A 44-year-old woman with heart failure diagnosed 9 months ago is evaluated for 3-month history of
non- productive cough. No history of chest pain, dyspnoea or orthopnoea. She has never smoked.
Her current medications are lisinopril, carvedialol and fruosemide. Unremarkable cardiac and chest
examination (see reports). Blood pressure 100/70 mmHg
Heart rate 76 /min
Respiratory rate 18/min
Oxygen saturation 95 %
Chest X-ray: Normal
ECHO: Showed left ventricular ejection fracture 40%.
Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
A. Discontinue lisinopril
B. Order pulmonary function test
C. Increase the dose of fruosemide
D. Start inhaled B2- adrenergic agonist
extra_note: In other recalls A is “stop Furosemide”so we went with B.

front_raw:
A 45-year-old man has been diagnosed as a case of pulmonary tuberculosis. which of the following
investigations is essential prior initiation of the therapy?
A. Vitamin B6
B. PPD skin test
C. Plasma glucose
D. Liver function test

A 39-year-old man came to the clinic for follow-up. He is recently diagnosed as pulmonary
tuberculosis and was started on rifampicin, Isoniazid, pyrazinamide and ethambutol for 4 weeks.
Basic lab workup were normal. LFT test was repeated (see lab results).
Test Result Normal Values
Direct bilirubin 56 1.5-6.5 mol/L
Total bilirubin 76 3.5-16.5 mol/L
Aspartate aminotransferase 465 12-40 IU/L
Alanine aminotransferase 620 5-40 IU/L
Alkaline phosphatase 720 39-117 IU/L
Gamma glutamyltransferase 387 6 to 37 1U/L
Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
A. Stop Isoniazid
B. Stop rifampicin
C. Stop pyrazinamide
D. Stop all medications
extra_note: Increased LFTs by five folds

front_raw:
A 54-year-old man presents with shortness of breath and fever for 1 week. On physical examination,
the patient is febrile and dyspneic. His oxygen's saturation is 89% on room air. Chest examination
shows absent breath sounds and dullness to percussion over right lung field. Chest radiography
confirms a large right-sided pleural effusion. Which of the following is the most useful to establish a
diagnosis of exudative pleural effusion?
A. Pleural fluid protein/ serum protein < 0.5
B. Pleural fluid pLDH/ serum LDH > 0.6
C. Pleural fluid LDH >1/3 normal upper limit for serum
D. Pleural fluid white cell count > 1000

A 54-year-old man presents with shortness of breath and fever for 1 week. On physical examination,
the patient is febrile and dyspneic. His oxygen's saturation is 89% on room air Chest examination
shows absent breath sounds and dullness to percussion over right lung field. Chest radiography
confirms a large right-sided pleural effusion. Which of the following factors indicating the need for
therapeutic thoracentesis?
A. Loculated pleural fluid
B. Pleural fluid pH more than 7.30
C. Pleural fluid glucose more than 80 mg/di
D. Negative gram stain of the pleural fluid

A 38-year-old man who is smoker for several years presents to the clinic with progressive shortness
of breath. Pulmonary function test (PFT) done which results in the following parameters: forced
expiratoy volume (FEV1/forced vital capacity (FVC) ratio < 0.7 with minimal improvement after
bronchodilators low diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO).
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A. Emphysema
B. Bronchial asthma
C. Chronic bronchitis
D. Interstitial lung disease

A 50-year-old man presents to the clinic with chronic history of productive cough and shortness of
breath. A diagnosis of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is suspected. Pulmonary
function test is ordered. Which of the following pulmonary function tests is most likely to represent
COPD?
A. Increased total lung capacity (TLC), decreased vital capacity (VC), decreased FEV1/FVC ratio
B. Increased total lung capacity (TLC), decreased vital capacity (VC), increased FEV1/FVC ratio
C. Decreased total lung capacity (TLC), increased vital capacity (VC), decreased FEV1/FVC ratio
D. Increased total lung capacity (TLC), normal vital capacity (VC), decreased FEV1/FVC ratio.

A 35-year-old-man presented to the Emergency Department with 5-day history of fever, shortness of
breath and productive cough. Lung examination reveals duliness to percussion to approximately half
of the lung field on the right and his breath sounds are markedly diminished. Chest radiography,
shows right lower and middle lobes consolidation with moderate pleural effusion.
Which of the following would indicate the need for tube thoracostomy?
A. Pleural fluid glucose below 60 mg/di
B. Pleural fluid PH more than 7.20
C. Pleural fluid with more than 90% polymorphonucleocytes (PMNs)
D. Pleural fluid/ serum protein less than 0.4

A 36-year-old man presents to Emergency Department with 5-day history of fever, productive cough
and shortness of breath. On examination, he is febrile with temperature 38.5 C and his lung
examination reveals dullness to percussion with markedly diminished breath sound over half of the
lung field on the right side. Chest radiography shows right lower and middle lobes consolidation and
moderate pleural effusion. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
A. Start azithromycin and ceftriaxone
B. Start azithromycin, ceftriaxone and oseltamivir
C. Start azithromycin, ceftriaxone and do thoracocentesis
D. Start azithromycin, ceftriaxone and do CT scan of the chest

A 36-year-old man presents to Emergency Department with 4-week history of low-grade fever, non-
productive cough and shortness of breath. On examination, he is febrile with temperature 37.9 °C
and his lung examination reveals duliness to percussion with markedly diminished breath sound over
half of the lung field on the right side. A diagnosis of tuberculous pleural effusion is suspected. Chest
radiography shows moderate pleural effusion (see lab results).
Test Result Normal Values
Leukocytes 4500 <1000/pL
Total Protein 6 10-20 g/L
Glucose 1.6 >2.2 mmol/L
LDH 650 <200/UL
Which of the following tests is the most sensitive to establish the diagnosis?
A. Positive pleural fluid AB culture
B. Exudative pleural fluid with lymphocytosis
C. Pleural fluid with very low glucose concentration
D. Pleural fluid adenosine deaminase more than 45 IU/L

A patient with a diagnosis of advanced chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) who is
discussing with his doctor the therapeutic benefits of different therapies on his survival rate Which of
the following therapies is most likely to improve his survival?
A. Theophylline
B. Corticosteroids
C. Mucolytics
D. Oxygen

A 25-year-old man presents to the Emergency Department with progressive shortness of breath,
non- productive cough and wheezes for 1 day. On examinations, he has obvious difficulty in
breathing and his lungs show with diffuse wheezes but no crackles. Blood pressure 120/70 mmHg,
Heart rate 100 /min, Respiratory rate 28 /min, Temperature 36.6 °C, Oxygen saturation 93 %
Which of the following is the most effective initial treatment at this time?
A. Epinephrine
B. Inhaled steroids
C. Inhaled B2 agonists
D. Intravenous magnesium

A 25-year-old woman non-smoker presents to Emergency Department with sudden onset of severe
chest pain and shortness of breath. Her past medical history is significant for caesarean section 4
days ago. Her examinations show a distressed woman with oxygen saturation 92% but otherwise
unremarkable. Chest radiography is unremarkable.
Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
A. Start warfarin
B. Start thrombolytic drugs
C. Start low molecular heparin
D. Insert inferior vena caval filter

A 76-year-old man with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) comes to the clinic for a
follow-up. He is currently taking salmeterol, using albuterol rescue inhaler 2 to 3 times per day for
the past 3 months. He has been hospitalized for COPD exacerbations twice in the past 6 months.
Which of the following medications should be added to the maintenance regimen?
A. Montelukast
B. Prednisone
C. Tiotropium
D. Formoterol

A 30-year-old woman presents with recurrent attacks of dyspnea and cough when exposed to dust
and perfumes. Physical examination is normal except for mild expiratory wheeze on lung auscultation
(see report).
Spirometry: Reversible bronchospasm.
Which of the following is most appropriate to initiate at this stage?
A. Inhaled tiotropium
B. Inhaled salbutamol
C. Inhaled budesonide
D. Montelukast

A 60-year-old man with a history of 20-pack-year smoking presents with exertional dyspnea and
productive cough for 3 months. He had similar attack last year. On examination, he has central
cyanosis and expiratory wheeze on lung auscultation (see lab resuits)
Test Result Normal Values
ABG HCO3- 36 22-28 mmol/L
ABG PCO2 7.7 4.7-6.0 kPa
рН 7.35 7.36-7.45
ABG P02 8.4 10.6-14.2 kPa
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A. Bronchial asthma
B. Chronic bronchitis
C. Pulmonary embolism
D. Interstitial pulmonary fibrosis

A 70-year-old man heavy smoker, presents with left sided chest pain and hemoptysis for 2 days.
Recently his son has noticed change in the quality of his father's voice. On examination, he has early
digital clubbing and both of his wrists are painful and tender.
Blood pressure 110/70 mmHg
Heart rate 85 /min
Respiratory rate 22 /min
Temperature 36.6 °C
Oxygen saturation 92 %
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A. Tuberculosis
B. Bronchiectasis
C. Pulmonary embolism
D. Bronchogenic carcinoma

In a patient with acute asthmatic attack, which of the following is the most recommended tool to
assess the response to therapy?
A.Chest radiography
B. Arterial blood gas
C. Pulsus paradoxus
D. Peak flow meter

A 65-year-old smoker is being evaluated for pleural effusion. He has cough, dyspnea and hemoptysis.
On examination, signs of massive pleural effusion are present on right side but the trachea and apex
beat are not shifted.
Which of the following explains these clinical findings?
A. Heart failure
B. Tubercular pleural effusion
C. Effusion due to esophageal rupture
D. Carcinoma, obstructing ipsilateral main bronchus

A 45-year-old man is diagnosed to have pulmonary tuberculosis for which he was started on 4 anti-
tuberculous drugs 2 months ago. During routine follow up, his blood work shows hyperuricemia (see
lab result).
Test Result Normal Values
Uric acid 600 200-410 mol/L (Male)
140-360 mol/L (Female)
What anti-TB drug is responsible for this finding?
A. Isoniazid
B. Rifampicin
C. Ethambutol
D. Pyrazinamide

A 32-year-old man is seen in the clinic for evaluation of primary infertility. Past medical history is
significant for recurrent sinusitis. Sperm analysis shows normal number of sperms, but they are
immotile (see report).
Chest radiography: shows situs inversus.
Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A. Cystic fibrosis
B. Kartagener's syndrome
C. Wegner's granulomatosis
D. Good pasture's syndrome

A 40-year-old man presents to the Emergency Department complaining of progressive dyspnea over
5 days. Past medical history is significant for road traffic accident 2 week ago. Lung auscultation
revealed absent breath sounds in the right side (see image and lab results).
Blood pressure 100/70 mmH
Heart rate 90 /min
Respiratory rate 24 /min
Temperature 36.6 °C
Oxygen saturation 90 %
Test Result Normal Values
Hb 90 130-170 g/L (Male)
120-160 g/L (Female)
WBC 6 4.5-10.5 x 109/L
Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
A. Antibiotics
B. Anticoagulation
C. Chest tube insertion
D. Salbutamol nebulizer

A male farmer with chronic liver disease secondary to repeated infections of schistosoma mansoni
complains of progressive dyspnea. Examination revealed elevated JVP, clear lung fields and left
parasternal heave.
What is the likely complication that has occurred?
A. Bronchiectasis
B. Pulmonary embolism
C. Constrictive pericarditis
D. Pulmonary hypertension

A 45-year-old man presents with 5-year history of cough, productive of large volume of sputum
associated with dyspnea and hemoptysis. On examination, he has clubbing and course crackles in the
right base. Which of the following tests has the highest diagnostic value?
A. X-ray chest
B. Bronchoscopy
C. High resolution CT chest
D. Pulmonary function tests

A 50-year-old woman with pulmonary hypertension is being evaluated for a possibility of chronic
thromboembolic disease. Which of the following investigations has the highest diagnostic value?
A. Echocardiogram
B. Electrocardiography
C. Spiral CT chest with contrast
D. Ventilation-perfusion lung scan

Which of the following drugs is a leukotriene receptor antagonist?
A. Infliximab
B. Tenofovir
C. Montelukast
D. Voriconazole

According to the World Health Organization classification of pulmonary hypertension, which of the
following conditions falls under group 3?
A. Portal hypertension
B. Left ventricular failure
C. Chronic thromboembolic disease
D. Lung fibrosis with chronic hypoxemia

A 55-year-old man presents with progressive dyspnea and cough for 6 weeks. He is a heavy smoker. 2
weeks ago, he started having headaches and noticed swelling of his face. Physical examination
reveals prominent non-pulsating neck veins, puffiness of the face and edema of the upper limbs (see
report).
Chest X-ray: Shows a prominence of the right hilum.
Which of the following types of lung cancer is the most commonly associated with this clinical
presentation?
A. Adenocarcinoma of the lung
B. Carcinoid tumor of the lung
C. Squamous cell lung cancer
D. Small cell lung cancer

An asymptomatic 60-year-old man, non-smoker presents for a routine annual physical check- up. A
chest X-ray showed an opacity, which is less than 3 cm in the left upper lobe.
which of the following is the next best step in the management?
A. Surgical resection
B. Review old chest X-ray
C. CT chest with IV contrast
D. CT-guided transthoracic needle biopsy

A 55-year old man with stable COPD, presents with sudden onset left-sided pleuritic chest pain and
exertional dyspnea. On examination, he is not in distress. the trachea is central and breath sounds
are equal in both sides with occasional mild expiratory wheezes (see report).
Blood pressure 130/70 mmHg
Heart rate 80 /min
Respiratory rate 22 /min
Temperature 36.6 °C
Oxygen saturation 93 %
Chest X-ray: Shows a left sided pneumothorax measuring 2 cm between the lung and chest wall.
Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
A. Needle aspiration
B. Chest tube insertion
C. Perform pleurodesis
D. Oxygenation and observation
extra_note: Because the patient is vitally stable, and Apex-Cupola distance is less than 3 cm.

front_raw:
A 20-year-old woman presents to the Out-Patient Department with mild dyspnea, malaise, low-grade
fever and arthralgia. Physical examination showed tender erythematous nodules measuring 2-3 cm
in both shins. Chest auscultation revealed fine basal crackles. Which of the following is the next best
action in management?
A. Blood culture
B. Oral steroids
C. Chest X-ray
D. Skin biopsy
extra_note: Beware that most diagnostic is Biopsy from the most accessible lesion (eg. skin)

front_raw:
Which of the following is the best oxygen delivery system in a patient with Chronic Obstructive
Pulmonary Disease?
A. Simple face mask
B. Rebreathing bag
C. Nasal cannula
D. Venturi mask

A 65-year-old man known to have COPD presented to the Emergency Department with increasing
dyspnea, cough, expectoration and fever. Initial assessment revealed fully conscious patient with
mild distress, central cyanosis and bilateral wheezing on chest auscultation. The patient was started
on high flow oxygen and salbutamol nebulizer but 1 hour later, his level of consciousness is reduced
(see lab result)
Test Result Normal Values
ABG HCO3. 36 22-28 mmol/L
ABG PCO2 9 4.7-6.0 kPa
pH 7.18 7.36-7.45
ABG PO2 15 10.6-14.2 kPa
Which of the following is the best initial step in management?
A. Start mechanical ventilation
B. Reduce oxygen flow
C. Order brain CT scan
D. Give naloxone

A 30-year-old postpartum woman is admitted to the General Ward with diagnosis of right leg DVT.
She was started on enoxaparin 80 mg bid, but in the same day of admission, she developed sudden
onset dyspnea and right pleuritic chest pain. On examination, she was dyspneic and apprehensive.
Heart sounds showed loud P2 and lungs were clear to auscultation (see lab results and report).
Blood pressure 125/70 mmHg Heart rate 100 /min Respiratory rate 22 /min Temperature 36.6 °C
Oxygen saturation 95 %
Test Result Normal Values
ABG HCO3- 22 22-28 mmol/L
ABG PCO2 4.2 4.7-6.0 kPa
pH 7.48 7.36-7.45
ABG PO2 12 10.6-14.2 kPa
Spiral CT chest: Thrombus in the right lower pulmonary artery. Which of the following is the most
appropriate step in management?
A. Change enoxaparin to sodium heparin
B. Treat with thrombolytic therapy
C. Continue the same management
D. Perform invasive thrombectomy

A 40-year-old man with paraplegia following road traffic accident one year ago is brought to the
Emergency Department because of sudden onset dyspnea and chest pain. On examination, he is in
severe distress and cyanosed. He has left parasternal heave and loud P2. Chest is clear to
auscultation (see lab results and reports).
